_doc: P34 NAS metadata catalog — OBSERVED reality recorded as DATA, not hardcoded in code.
_principle: Operator directive 2026-07-21: do NOT over-hardcode / over-hard-parse. Rigid regexes make real
material unfindable because the lab's naming is inconsistent. Instead: record what is ACTUALLY
observed (patterns + counterexamples + samples + coverage) here, and let code match tolerantly,
guided by this catalog. A new convention should be a catalog edit, never a code change.
Never hardcode a /Volumes/... path: the volume name depends on mount order (resolve at runtime).
_key_convention: Keys beginning with '_' are documentation for humans. Consumers MUST skip them when iterating (e.g. `for init, rec in catalog['initials'].items() if not init.startswith('_')`).

confidence_levels.assumed: inferred from a single observation, a document, or reasoning. Do NOT build a hard gate on these.

mount.resolve_rule: Do NOT hardcode a volume name. macOS mounts SMB per-user mode-700; a second mount of the same share gets '-1', a third '-2'. Resolve by probing /Volumes/* for a directory that contains BOTH 'GRM/' and 'MM/'.

observed_mounts_2026_07_22.note: another user's mount — mode-700, not readable by us. Probing for GRM/+MM/ correctly rejects it.

mount.auth_note: ONE attempt only; the NAS auto-bans repeated logins. Never re-auth or re-mount from an agent. If no /Volumes entry qualifies, FAIL LOUDLY — do not try to mount.
mount.concurrency_note: Max ~3 concurrent NAS readers. Prefer one sequential pass; sample to confirm rather than re-crawling.

unicode._doc: The single most common silent-miss class on this share.
unicode.rule: NFC-normalise BOTH sides before any filename comparison, regex match, dict key, or DB write. `unicodedata.normalize('NFC', name)`.
unicode.why: Python's \w and [^\W\d_] exclude combining marks (category Mn), so a NFD 'Á' (A + U+0301) fails an ASCII-ish name regex.
also_applies_to: every other subtree, not just Memory/Papers

never_descend.name: CSNL_new-1
never_descend.why: SELF-REFERENTIAL SYMLINK at share root -> /Volumes/CSNL_new-1. Any followed walk recurses forever.

never_descend.name: #recycle
never_descend.why: Synology recycle bin — a full SHADOW COPY of the tree (649, GRM, MM, Memory, Server, ...). Doubles every count.

never_descend.name: @Recycle
never_descend.why: QNAP recycle bin — second shadow copy (GRM, Grant, Server, people, results, zz.nii 424MB)

walk_rules.os_walk_hint: os.walk(base, followlinks=False) then `dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in PRUNE]`, and wrap iteration in try/OSError so an EACCES subtree warns instead of aborting.

matching_policy._doc: How code should USE this catalog. The point of the catalog is that these are knobs in data, not branches in code.
order: 2. Apply ignore_rules (lock stub / dotfile / extension allow-list).
3. Tokenise the stem on [_\-. ()]+ — do NOT anchor a regex to ^ or $. Both token orders occur ('260715_JOP' and 'JOP_260701').
4. Find a date token by trying directories.<x>.date_token_forms IN ORDER (most specific first) and stop at the first form that yields any date — otherwise '2025.08.14' is re-read as YY.MM.DD.
5. Find an initial token by whole-token match against initials{} (aliases included), case-insensitively; also try korean_name and romanised_name.
6. Prefer the FOLDER date over the filename date where both exist — filename yy is frequently wrong (250225_AIWorkshop.pptx sits in 20260225; JSL_240422.pptx in 20260422).
never: Never require a leading-initial prefix — it loses SK 27→1, JSL 24→8, SMJ 25→7 (measured on PaperBlitz source_files).
Never require an anchored `$` after the date — 'JOP_260325_part1.pptx' and 'MSY_260422_MSY.key' both break.
Never match a kind token as a substring — 'AIGRM' contains 'grm' and manufactures presenter_name='AIGRM'.
Never coin a presenter from an unknown token — 'special', 'Special', 'AIGRM' all became fake presenters this way.
Never treat 'no extractable text / no filename token' as 'no material'.
